prompt.en: An HF tuner has only an unbalanced output, but the antenna will be fed with window line. Where should the balanced-to-unbalanced device go?

text.en: At the tuner output before the window line begins
At any random point along the balanced line
Only at the antenna feed point after the window-line run
At the microphone connector because that is inside the station

explanation.en: The transition belongs where balanced and unbalanced parts meet; in this setup, that is where the unbalanced tuner output hands off to the window line.

prompt.en: Why is open-wire line usually kept away from metal gutters and railings?

text.en: Metal nearby can disturb the fields and change the line behaviour.
Metal nearby turns the route into a better balanced-line support.
The line needs nearby metal to set its velocity factor.
Keeping it near metal is the normal way to reduce line loss.

explanation.en: Balanced line depends on geometry and surrounding fields; nearby conductors can upset the balance and impedance.

prompt.en: A dipole is fed with coax. Where is the balanced-to-unbalanced transition normally handled?

text.en: At the antenna feed point with a suitable balun or choke arrangement
By adding extra coax length anywhere in the run

explanation.en: The feed point is where the balanced antenna meets the unbalanced coax, so that is the natural place to handle the transition.
